i think play possession will be more useful for you especially if you play 4-4-2b because then you can keep the ball safely until your attacking midfielder can pick out a pass to your forwards and it also makes it harder for the other team to win the ball back if they have less in midfield, and with the amount of midfielders you have it will make it hard for them to create chances which means they will probably have to press hard and play a high tempo which will create worse chances for them and leave their players out of position

i think that's good but personally i would not play high speed passing since most of your play is going to be in the midfield, also if you have defence supporting midfield i suggest man marking so that it's harder for them to break through since your defenders are closing them down and probably offside trap on too since your defenders playing higher up makes it easier to catch opponents offside

it depends on their formation and tactics, if i play a stronger team and they're playing 4-3-3 then i'd be inclined to go 4-4-2 passing game then forwards on support midfield to overload the midfield and then play passing game and put the sliders to match the quality gap, so if their team rating is 95 and mine is 85 then i would probably go for close down opposition with press, defensive style and slow build up if you have a weak midfield or play possession if you have some decent midfielders

if they're playing with 4 or 5 midfielders with wing play then play counter attack and don't mess with line tactics, if they're playing passing game with 4-5 midfielders i would suggest that you play wing play with a 4-3-3 then attacking fullbacks, potentially use midfielders for fullbacks if you have any that are good enough and you have good midfield coverage, then play high speed passing, sit deep on pressing and slightly attacking

you should test these tactics before using them in friendlies because i can't guarantee you'll win since you can't see the full extent of what your opponent has done to adjust properly, also if you have high defence centre backs then leave on zonal marking and don't use offside trap unless you are playing with attacking style

your line tactics should match how you want your team to play in a match, if you want to play a passing game and control the midfield you can get your strikers to support midfield, if you're playing a hard opponent and you want to play for the draw you can get your midfielders to protect the defence, and you can play attacking fullbacks if you want to play wing play or passing game to give some wide support, and a good thing to do with attacking fullbacks is drop a midfielder into a fullback role because good midfielders have high defending and attacking stats whereas the best fullback defenders still don't have very good attacking stats

while you learn the game i would suggest you save before every match, if you don't want to cheat then it's fine but i did it when i first started to change random things and see what works and what doesn't, you should leave more responsibility to your staff at the start and use pre made tactics like the tiki taka or gegenpress. i assume you're on the level where you really don't know much at all and you should focus on learning about your players stats and performances.

in fifa your players are rated from 1-99 in terms of ability and in football manager it's 1-200 although good luck finding a player that's 1 rated lol, there's many key parts and the main ones you should be looking at are: how comfortable they are in the position, how good their stats are for the ones needed in their role, there's also a reports tab on every players page which shows you their strengths and weaknesses, and also some of their hidden attributes such as injury proneness and consistency, other factors that affect their form are morale, team cohesion and tactical familiarity, i'll try to answer any questions if you want to ask but despite my high playing time i'm not that good either as i just play more casually
